More from the workshop

Apps to use. Games to play. Productivity sold separately.

Project

jobsearch.quest — your AI job-search council

Job searching alone is brutal. This runs the proven "Never Search Alone" method — but solo: an AI council holds your weekly job-search meeting (wins, blockers, the hot seat, real commitments for next week) so you don't have to wrangle five humans onto a call. Sign in to start your first session free.

↗
Project

H100s & Burn Rate — the album

Twenty-three original songs that started as places on a world map. Press play for “A Million Open Windows,” choose any track, or send someone a link straight to your favorite.

↗
Project

AutoDJ · Switchback

A 15-minute electronic mix for a focus session or a workout. Four original tracks crossfade as the pace rises and settles. A two-note bell tells you when the session is over. Play, skip to a chapter, or download the MP3.

↗
Project

City Picker — where should you live?

If you work remotely, the world is the menu. Set your salary and put your priorities in order to see how 17 cities rank. The savings estimates use November 2025 household budgets.

↗
Project

NomadVibe — find a city for your household

Compare 65 cities against your household budget, working hours and local job needs. See exactly why a city qualifies or misses, then change one assumption and try again. Costs are estimates and job examples are dated.

↗
Project

LinkedIn Translator

Type something honest in plain English and get back peak LinkedIn cringe — 🚀 synergy, humble-brags, the works. The public version uses phrase rules in your browser.

↗
Project

Grand Kitchen Tour — pickleball as a campaign RPG

Pickleball in the shape of Baldur's Gate 3. Recruit a party of misfits, fight through six story chapters, earn XP and loot, and face the Sovereign Picklewhip. Every shot is a dice roll; every win levels you up. Beat it and there's a New Game+. The most complete game I've built.

↗
Project

DINK — pickleball as a card game

You and the computer each start with a dink, a drive, and a lob. Match a shot and your hand shrinks. Counter it and you draw a card. Leave your opponent without a reply to score. First to five wins.

↗
Project

Pickle: Mind Game

Ten pickleball decisions, four ways to play each ball. Read the court, choose your shot and aim, then see why a middle reset, a speed-up or a block fits that particular rally. Replay the ones you missed.

↗
Project

Pickleball d20 — the tactical version

The turn-based, stat-based take: doubles where court position, the two-bounce rule, and kitchen faults all genuinely matter, and a 20-sided die decides whether your shot lands. Closer to chess than to arcade.

Still on the workbench 5 experiments

Unfinished or parked. These aren’t available to try yet, but the ideas are worth keeping.

Private pilot

Weekly Check-in Generator

Turn messy notes into a seven-section weekly update. The private editor keeps drafts in your browser and exports Markdown. A configured installation can also save to Notion.

Markdown export · Optional Gemini and Notion integrations

In progress

Directory — my week, written by itself

A small command-line tool that writes my week for me: it pulls my Claude Code sessions, git commits, and GitHub activity, summarizes them, and publishes a tidy digest to Notion. Replaces the manual retro. It's a CLI, not a site — just needs a README and a schedule.

TypeScript · Node CLI · Notion API  —  to finish: README + cron

Parked

Voice Clone Lab

A small rig for benchmarking what actually makes a cloned voice sound like you — word-error-rate, real-time speed, and a dashboard for rating naturalness. Built for a workshop; would make a good essay on what's hard about voice cloning.

Python · OmniVoice · WER/RTF eval  —  could become: an essay + the dashboard

Parked

Bittersweet Symphony, humanized

MIDI experiments to make a stiff string cover breathe — nudging timing off the grid, lifting the solo out of the mix. Scripts and audio, no front end. A rabbit hole I enjoyed.

Python · MIDI · SoundFont  —  needs: a way to hear the before/after in a browser

Parked

Pickleball video analysis — an honest failure

I tried to break down phone-recorded matches with vision models — rallies, shots, player stats. It mostly doesn't work, and I wrote down exactly why single-camera vision falls apart. Kept it because the post-mortem is the useful part.

Python · VLM pipeline  —  verdict: wearables/court sensors, not phone cameras
